record.title: The polynomial-time recognition conjecture for reduced clique graphs of chordal graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $C_R(G)$ denote its reduced clique graph. A graph is **chordal** if it has no induced cycle of length at least four. The recognition problem asks whether a given graph is isomorphic to $C_R(G)$ for some chordal graph $G$.

**Reduced clique graph recognition conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a given graph is isomorphic to $C_R(G)$ for some chordal graph $G$.

Polynomial-time recognition is known for clique graphs of chordal graphs, but the source says that the corresponding techniques do not obviously extend to reduced clique graphs. The conjectured algorithm is therefore presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew and Andrew Probert, “Reduced clique graphs: a correction to "Chordal graphs and their clique graphs"”, arXiv:2301.03781 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03781

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Scott and Seymour's tournament-local chromatic number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Scott and Seymour's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ there exists a positive integer $\chi$ such that, for every graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geqslant \chi$ and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there is a vertex $v$ such that

$$
\chi(G[N_T^+(v)])\geqslant k.
$$

The paper disproves this conjecture, so the proposed implication does not hold in general.
record.source_name: António Girão, Kevin Hendrey, Freddie Illingworth, Florian Lehner, Lukas Michel, Michael Savery and Raphael Steiner, “Chromatic number is not tournament-local”, arXiv:2305.15585 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15585

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2023). “This conjecture remained open for two decades and was first proved by Lov\'{a}sz using homotopy theory (see also B\'{a}r\'{a}ny and Greene for very short proofs).”

record.title: The radial tree-width conjecture for graphs excluding quasi-geodesic subdivisions of the triangle
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. For $c,k\in\mathbb{N}$, a **$c$-quasi-geodesic $(\geqslant ck)$-subdivision of $K^3$** means a subdivision of the triangle whose subdivided paths are $c$-quasi-geodesic and have length at least $ck$. The **radial tree-width** of $G$ is the tree-width notion defined for radial decompositions.

**Radial tree-width conjecture.** There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, if a connected graph $G$ does not contain a $c$-quasi-geodesic $(\geqslant ck)$-subdivision of $K^3$ for some $c,k\in\mathbb{N}$, then

$$
\operatorname{radial\ tree\text{-}width}(G)\leqslant f(k).
$$

The preceding discussion explains that the subdivided-star argument does not directly produce a quasi-geodesic structural subgraph and presents this assertion as an unresolved question for trees. No resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Sandra Albrechtsen, Reinhard Diestel, Ann-Kathrin Elm, Eva Fluck, Raphael W. Jacobs, Paul Knappe and Paul Wollan, “A structural duality for path-decompositions into parts of small radius”, arXiv:2307.08497 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08497

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

record.title: The fixed--modular integer programming tractability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\Delta \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be fixed. An integer program of the form (IP) has a constraint matrix $B$ that is **$\Delta$-modular** if its full-rank minors have absolute value at most $\Delta$ and at least one has absolute value $\Delta$.

**Fixed-$\Delta$ tractability conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm to solve any integer program of the form (IP) with a $\Delta$-modular constraint matrix.

This conjecture extends the polynomial-time solvability of totally unimodular integer programs to every fixed bound on the maximal non-vanishing subdeterminants. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Björn Kriepke, Gohar M. Kyureghyan and Matthias Schymura, “On the size of integer programs with bounded non-vanishing subdeterminants”, arXiv:2309.03772 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03772

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Langhede and Thomassen's exponential correspondence-colouring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. A **correspondence assignment** $(L,M)$ for $G$ consists of a list assignment $L$ and, for each edge, a partial matching between the corresponding vertex-colour pairs; an $(L,M)$-colouring chooses a colour from each list while avoiding matched pairs on every edge. The class of planar graphs has exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings if there exists a constant $c>0$ such that every planar graph $G$ and every $5$-correspondence assignment $(L,M)$ admit at least $2^{c\cdot v(G)}$ distinct $(L,M)$-colourings.

**Langhede and Thomassen's conjecture.** Planar graphs have exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings.

This conjecture asks for an exponential strengthening of the known $5$-correspondence-colourability of planar graphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Luke Postle and Evelyne Smith-Roberge, “Exponentially Many Correspondence Colourings of Planar and Locally Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2309.17291 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17291

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Anti-Sidorenko orientations conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be an undirected tree, and call an orientation of $T$ **tournament anti-Sidorenko** when it has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.

**Anti-Sidorenko orientations conjecture for trees.** For every undirected tree, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.
The paper says that this conjecture is affirmatively resolved for a special family of trees, while a complete characterization is not obtained; the general assertion therefore remains open.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox, Zoe Himwich, Nitya Mani and Yunkun Zhou, “Variations on Sidorenko's conjecture in tournaments”, arXiv:2402.08418 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08418

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “The general conjecture remains open, but a variety of special cases have been resolved.”

record.title: The generalized edge reconstruction conjecture
record.statement: Let $n\geq 4$, and let $G_1,\dots,G_k$ be a collection of $n$-edged graphs for some $k\geq 1$. Write $\coprod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ED}(G_i)$ for the disjoint union of their edge decks. **Generalized edge reconstruction conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$, the collection $\{G_1,\dots,G_k\}$ is uniquely reconstructible from $\coprod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ED}(G_i)$. This is explicitly disproved in the paper: for every $n\geq 2$, some finite collection is not reconstructible, so the conjecture is false.
record.source_name: Maxine E. Calle and Julian J. Gould, “A combinatorial K-theory perspective on the Edge Reconstruction Conjecture in graph theory”, arXiv:2402.14986 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14986

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Grzesik–Lee–Lidický–Volec conjecture on apices of Sidorenko graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with the Sidorenko property. For an integer $k$, the **$k$-apex** of $G$ is obtained by adding $k$ independent vertices, each adjacent to every vertex of $G$. **Grzesik–Lee–Lidický–Volec conjecture.** The $k$-apex of $G$ is common for every $k$. This conjecture concerns the classification of common graphs, where a graph is common when its Ramsey multiplicity equals the random-coloring benchmark. The paper proves the assertion for $k\leq 5$ when $G$ is a tree, while the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Daniel Kráľ, Matjaž Krnc and Ander Lamaison, “Ramsey multiplicity of apices of trees”, arXiv:2403.15808 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15808

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Harary's edge reconstruction conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a finite simple graph with $|E|>4$. For each edge of $G$, let $G_i$ denote the maximal subgraph obtained by deleting that edge, and define the **edge deck** of $G$ by

$$
\operatorname{Deck}(G)\coloneqq\{G_i\}_{i=1}^m.
$$

**Harary's reconstruction conjecture.** If $\operatorname{Deck}(G)=\operatorname{Deck}(H)$ for some graph $H$, then $G\cong H$.

This conjecture asserts that every graph with more than four edges is uniquely determined, up to isomorphism, by its maximal edge-deleted subgraphs. The paper proves it for graphs with exactly one cycle and three non-isomorphic subtrees; the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Anthony E. Pizzimenti and Umarkhon Rakhimov, “Reconstructing edge-deleted unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:2411.03133 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03133

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: Thomassen's conjecture on balanced clique subdivisions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $d(G)$ denote its average degree, and let a **balanced $K_t$-subdivision** be a subdivision of $K_t$ in which all subdivided edge-paths have the same length. **Thomassen's conjecture.** For any constant $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a function $g(t)$ such that every graph $G$ with $d(G)\geq g(t)$ contains a balanced $K_t$-subdivision. This is posed as a strengthening related to Mader's conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Xia Wang, Donglei Yang, Fan Yang and Haotian Yang, “Topological cliques in sparse expanders”, arXiv:2411.12237 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.12237

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: DP-4-colorability conjecture for planar graphs without chorded 6-cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and suppose that $G$ contains no chorded $6$-cycle, meaning no cycle of length six with an edge joining two nonconsecutive vertices on the cycle. A graph is **DP-$4$-colorable** if every cover of $G$ admits a DP-coloring with four colors.

**DP-4-colorability conjecture.** Every planar graph without chorded $6$-cycles is DP-$4$-colorable.

The preceding results establish DP-$4$-colorability for a narrower class of planar graphs excluding specified configurations, but the paper does not prove the conjecture for all planar graphs without chorded $6$-cycles.
record.source_name: Huihui Fang, Danjun Huang, Tao Wang and Weifan Wang, “Variable degeneracy of planar graphs without chorded 6-cycles”, arXiv:2502.18089 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18089

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

record.title: Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture for graph homomorphism counts
record.statement: Let $Hom(F,G)$ denote the number of graph homomorphisms from $F$ to $G$, and let $\mathcal{G}$ be the family of all graphs. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, say that $Hom(\mathcal{F},\cdot)$ is reconstructible if, for every graph $G$ with at least three vertices, the vector of homomorphism counts $Hom(\mathcal{F},G)$ is uniquely determined by the vectors $Hom(\mathcal{F},G\setminus i)$ for every vertex $i$ of $G$. **Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture.** $Hom(\mathcal{G},\cdot)$ is reconstructible. This is the homomorphism-count formulation of the Ulam–Kelly graph reconstruction conjecture, asserting that a graph with at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the collection of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The source presents this formulation as a motivation and question; no resolution is given here.
record.source_name: Thomás Jung Spier, “Efficient reconstruction of the characteristic polynomial”, arXiv:2503.17853 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2502.12781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12781).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17853

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Generalized Erdős–Rogers polynomial-growth conjecture for hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ and $G$ be $r$-graphs, meaning $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $f_{F,G}(n)$ denote the generalized Erdős–Rogers number. An **$F$-iterated blowup** is the hypergraph obtained by repeatedly applying the blowup construction determined by $F$.

**Generalized Erdős–Rogers polynomial-growth conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(F,G)$ such that

$$
f_{F,G}(n)\ge n^c
$$

if and only if $G$ is a subgraph of an $F$-iterated blowup.

This extends the cited conjecture for $F=K^3_3$ to arbitrary $r$-graphs $F$ and $G$. The source proposes it as an extension, and no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Xiaoyu He and Jiaxi Nie, “Generalized Erdős-Rogers problems for hypergraphs”, arXiv:2504.03138 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: Nash-Williams' Chvátal-type conjecture for Hamilton cycles in digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph on $n\geq 3$ vertices, and let $d^+_1\leq\cdots\leq d^+_n$ and $d^-_1\leq\cdots\leq d^-_n$ be its ordered outdegree and indegree sequences. **Nash-Williams' conjecture.** If, for every $i<n/2$, 

$$
d^+_i\geq i+1\text{ or }d^-_{n-i}\geq n-i,
$$

and

$$
d^-_i\geq i+1\text{ or }d^+_{n-i}\geq n-i,
$$

then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. This is a directed analogue of Chvátal's best-possible degree-sequence condition; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Yulin Chang, Yangyang Cheng, Tianjiao Dai, Qiancheng Ouyang and Guanghui Wang, “An exact Ore-degree condition for Hamilton cycles in oriented graphs”, arXiv:2507.04273 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04273

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2025). “This conjecture has been confirmed asymptotically in .”

record.title: The minor-excluded-cover-graph dim-boundedness conjecture
record.statement: Let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices, and let a graph **exclude $K_t$ as a minor** if it has no graph minor isomorphic to $K_t$. The dimension of a poset $P$, denoted $\dim(P)$, is the least number of linear extensions whose intersection is $P$. A class of posets is **dim-bounded** if the dimensions of its members are bounded by a function of the indicated graph parameter. **The minor-excluded-cover-graph conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$, the class of posets with cover graphs excluding $K_t$ as a minor is dim-bounded. This statement is presented as a conjectural generalization of the planar cover-graph and bounded-treewidth results described in the paper. The supplied text gives supporting context but no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Heather Smith Blake, Jędrzej Hodor, Piotr Micek, Michał T. Seweryn and William T. Trotter, “Planarity and dimension I”, arXiv:2510.18603 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18603

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

record.title: Cocks's hereditary treewidth–clique boundedness conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a hereditary graph class. A graph $H$ is $H$-free in $\mathcal{G}$ when graphs in the relevant subclass have no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The class $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if there is a function of clique number that bounds treewidth throughout $\mathcal{G}$. **Cocks's conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ excludes a complete bipartite graph and, for every non-complete graph $H\in\mathcal{G}$, the class of all $H$-free graphs in $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded. The source identifies this conjecture as still open and says that its pathwidth analogue follows from the paper's main theorem.
record.source_name: Sepehr Hajebi, “Polynomial bounds for pathwidth”, arXiv:2510.19120 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19120

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2025). “Chudnovsky and Trotignon refuted this conjecture in a strong sense, showing that neither polynomial nor any prescribed growth can be guaranteed in general.”

record.title: Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture on adding matching components
record.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph on two vertices. A pair $(G,H)$ is **Ramsey-finite** if it has only finitely many Ramsey-minimal graphs. **Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.** If $(G,H)$ is Ramsey-finite, then $(G\cup \ell K_2,H\cup mK_2)$ is Ramsey-finite for all integers $\ell,m\ge 0$. This conjecture concerns the stability of Ramsey-finiteness under adjoining arbitrary numbers of isolated matching components to the two target graphs. The paper states that this conjecture is true.
record.source_name: Yaping Mao, “Ramsey-finiteness for graph pairs: A complete solution to the Burr-Erdős-Faudree-Schelp conjectures”, arXiv:2604.17356 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17356

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2026). “The two 1981 conjectures are true, whereas Burr's stronger survey conjecture is false.”

record.title: Hardness conjecture for bounded-size inversion approximation
record.statement:
Let $p\geq 3$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. For a digraph $D$, let $\operatorname{sinv}_{k}^{\leq p}(D)$ denote the optimization problem of making $D$ $k$-arc-strong using inversions of size at most $p$.

**Bounded-size inversion approximation hardness conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, unless $P=NP$, for every $p\geq 3$ and every $k\geq 1$, no polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for $\operatorname{sinv}_{k}^{\leq p}$ in digraphs exists.

The conjecture asserts that increasing the allowed inversion size does not make the approximation problem easier. It is presented as an open conjecture in the source.
record.source_name: Florian Hörsch and Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta, “Increasing arc-connectivity by bounded- and fixed-size inversions”, arXiv:2604.22584 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22584

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “Also the parameterized complexity section leaves open questions.”

record.title: Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture for A-paths
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite or infinite graph and let $A\subseteq V(G)$. An **$A$-path** is a path in $G$ between two distinct vertices of $A$. Two subgraphs are at distance at least $r$ when the distance between their vertex sets is at least $r$. A set is **$(a,b)$-centered** if it is contained in the union of at most $a$ balls of radius at most $b$. **Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture.** There exist functions $f,g:\mathbb N\rightarrow\mathbb R$ such that for any $k,r\in\mathbb N$, graph $G$ and $A\subseteq V(G)$, either there exist $k$ $A$-paths pairwise at distance in $G$ at least $r$, or there exists a set $(f(k),g(r))$-centered in $G$ intersecting all $A$-paths. The conjecture is a coarse version of Gallai's packing-covering theorem for $A$-paths. The source does not state a resolution; its exact original formulation was reported as lost, and this is the formulation attributed to Geelen by Hendrey and Jacobs.
record.source_name: Chun-Hung Liu, “Coarse Menger property of quasi-minor excluded graphs and length spaces”, arXiv:2605.10068 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2512.17232](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17232).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10068

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Their counterexamples also disprove the cases for any pair $(k,r)$ with $k \geq 3$ and $r \geq 3$ and imply that Conjecture remains false even if the bound $cr$ for the radius of balls is changed to any function of $k$ and $r$.”

record.title: Georgakopoulos–Papasoglu fat minor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ and $G$ be graphs, let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ be a function. A graph is **$K$-fat-minor-free with respect to $X$** when it does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor.

**Fat minor conjecture.** For every graph $X$ there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ such that, for every graph $G$ and $K\in\mathbb{N}$, if $G$ does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor, then $G$ is $f(K)$-quasi-isometric to a graph with no $X$ minor.

This conjecture has been disproved, with further counterexamples showing failure even for certain small graphs and under a weakened conclusion. It is therefore refuted rather than open.
record.source_name: Sandra Albrechtsen, “A coarse Menger theorem for hyperbolic graphs, finitely presented groups, and more”, arXiv:2606.17605 (2026).
record.references:
